library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: Xiao AJ, Miller BW, Huntington JA, Nicolau DP. Ceftolozane/tazobactam
  pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic-derived dose justification for phase 3 studies
  in patients with nosocomial pneumonia. J Clin Pharmacol. 2016;56(1):56-66.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.566> (open access, PMC5049594)

The paper builds its dose justification in two steps, and both are packaged:

1. **Plasma-to-ELF kinetics in healthy volunteers** (Table 1). Plasma and
   bronchoalveolar-lavage epithelial lining fluid (ELF) concentrations from 25
   healthy adults were fitted, one model per drug, with a two-compartment
   plasma model plus an ELF compartment exchanging with the central
   compartment through two one-way clearances, `Qce` (in) and `Qec` (out). The
   ELF volume is fixed at 1 L, so the parametric penetration ratio is
   `PR = Qce / Qec`.
   Packaged as `Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy` and `Xiao_2016_tazobactam_healthy`.
2. **Simulation model for nosocomial pneumonia** (equations after 'The final
   PK model used in the Monte Carlo simulation'). The plasma PK of
   complicated intra-abdominal infection (cIAI) patients from the authors'
   earlier pooled analysis (Chandorkar 2015, packaged as
   `Chandorkar_2015_ceftolozane` / `Chandorkar_2015_tazobactam`) is combined
   with the healthy-volunteer ELF kinetics. Packaged as
   `Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia` and `Xiao_2016_tazobactam_pneumonia`.

```{r models}
mods <- c(
  "Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy", "Xiao_2016_tazobactam_healthy",
  "Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia", "Xiao_2016_tazobactam_pneumonia"
)
ui <- lapply(setNames(mods, mods), function(m) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(m)))
for (m in mods) cat(m, ":", ui[[m]]$description, "\n\n")
```

# Population

**Healthy-volunteer models.** 25 healthy adults (14 men, 11 women), median
[min, max] age 31 [21, 47] years, body weight 78 [56.5, 94.5] kg and
creatinine clearance (CrCL) 119 [77.7, 155.2] mL/min (Methods). Each received
ceftolozane/tazobactam 1.5 g (1000/500 mg) as a 60-minute infusion every 8
hours for three doses; 150 plasma and 25 ELF samples (one bronchoalveolar
lavage per subject, 1-8 h after the third dose) were analysed in NONMEM 7.2.

**Pneumonia simulation models.** No cohort was fitted. The plasma part is the
cIAI-patient model of Chandorkar 2015 (8 phase 1 and 2 phase 2 studies); the
ELF part is the healthy-volunteer fit above, assumed independent of the plasma
PK. The paper simulated 1000 patients per scenario with CrCL uniform on 90-150
mL/min (normal renal function), 30-50 (moderate) or 15-30 (severe impairment)
and body weight normal with mean 74 kg.

The same information is in each model's `population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy")()$population`.

# Part 1: plasma-to-ELF kinetics in healthy volunteers

## Penetration ratio: structural identity

In this structure `d/dt(elf) = Qce * Cc - Qec * Celf`, so over a steady-state
dosing interval the ELF:plasma AUC ratio equals `Qce / Qec` exactly. A
typical-value solve of each packaged model must reproduce the paper's
parametric PR (0.51 for ceftolozane, 0.46 for tazobactam).

```{r pr-identity}
ss_events <- function(dose) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 72, by = 8), amt = dose, rate = dose,
               evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(72, 80, by = 0.01), amt = 0, rate = 0,
               evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    mutate(CRCL = 119, WT = 70) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}
auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

pr_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(
  list(c("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy", 1000, 0.51),
       c("Xiao_2016_tazobactam_healthy", 500, 0.46)),
  function(x) {
    s <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui[[x[1]]]), ss_events(as.numeric(x[2])),
                         rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame") |>
      filter(time >= 72)
    th <- ui[[x[1]]]$theta
    data.frame(
      model = x[1],
      `Qce/Qec` = exp(th[["lq_c_elf"]] - th[["lq_elf_c"]]),
      `AUC ratio (simulated)` = auc_trap(s$time, s$Celf) / auc_trap(s$time, s$Cc),
      `PR (paper)` = as.numeric(x[3]),
      check.names = FALSE
    )
  }
))
knitr::kable(pr_tab, digits = 4)
stopifnot(
  # Same drawn (typical) parameters on both sides: pure numerical error.
  all(abs(pr_tab$`AUC ratio (simulated)` / pr_tab$`Qce/Qec` - 1) < 1e-3),
  # The paper's printed PR rounds Qce/Qec to two decimals.
  all(abs(pr_tab$`Qce/Qec` - pr_tab$`PR (paper)`) < 0.005)
)
```

## Penetration-ratio distribution

The paper reports the 5th, 25th, 75th and 95th percentiles of the model-
estimated PR distribution (Results). With log-normal IIV on `Qce`
(ceftolozane) or `Qec` (tazobactam), these follow from the typical PR and the
packaged variance alone.

```{r pr-percentiles}
pct <- c(0.05, 0.25, 0.75, 0.95)
pr_pct <- function(m, eta) {
  th <- ui[[m]]$theta
  sd <- sqrt(ui[[m]]$omega[eta, eta])
  # IIV on Qec enters the PR as exp(-eta); the percentiles are symmetric.
  exp(th[["lq_c_elf"]] - th[["lq_elf_c"]] + qnorm(pct) * sd)
}
pr_dist <- data.frame(
  percentile = paste0(pct * 100, "th"),
  ceftolozane_model = pr_pct("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy", "etalq_c_elf"),
  ceftolozane_paper = c(0.26, 0.39, 0.69, 1.02),
  tazobactam_model = pr_pct("Xiao_2016_tazobactam_healthy", "etalq_elf_c"),
  tazobactam_paper = c(0.21, 0.33, 0.64, 1.02)
)
knitr::kable(pr_dist, digits = 3)
# Largest gap 0.012 (ceftolozane 75th: 0.678 vs 0.69), consistent with the
# paper taking its percentiles from a simulated sample. Reading the variances
# as CV (sqrt) instead of log-scale variances moves the 5th/95th by > 0.1.
stopifnot(
  abs(pr_dist$ceftolozane_model - pr_dist$ceftolozane_paper) < 0.015,
  abs(pr_dist$tazobactam_model - pr_dist$tazobactam_paper) < 0.015
)
```

All eight percentiles agree with the paper within 0.012 (the largest gap, the
ceftolozane 75th percentile, 0.678 against 0.69, suggests the paper read its
percentiles from a simulated sample), which confirms that Table 1 reports log-scale variances (CV = sqrt(variance): 42%
and 48%, as stated in the text).

## Virtual healthy-volunteer cohort

```{r hv-cohort}
set.seed(2016)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)
n_hv <- 200
hv_cov <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(n_hv),
  CRCL = runif(n_hv, 77.7, 155.2),
  WT = runif(n_hv, 56.5, 94.5)
)
hv_events <- function(dose) {
  bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = hv_cov$id, time = c(0, 8, 16)) |>
      mutate(amt = dose, rate = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = hv_cov$id, time = 16 + c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.1), seq(2.25, 8, by = 0.25))) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    left_join(hv_cov, by = "id") |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
hv <- bind_rows(
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui$Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_healthy, hv_events(1000),
                  returnType = "data.frame") |> mutate(drug = "ceftolozane"),
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui$Xiao_2016_tazobactam_healthy, hv_events(500),
                  returnType = "data.frame") |> mutate(drug = "tazobactam")
) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 16) |>
  select(id, time, tad, drug, Cc, Celf)
```

```{r hv-plot, fig.cap = "Simulated plasma and ELF concentrations after the third 1.5 g dose in 200 virtual healthy volunteers (median and 5th-95th percentiles). Compare with the observed data of Figure 1 of Xiao 2016."}
hv |>
  filter(tad >= 0) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Celf), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(matrix = ifelse(matrix == "Cc", "Plasma", "ELF")) |>
  group_by(drug, matrix, tad) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, p50, colour = matrix, fill = matrix)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after third dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

As in Figure 1, the ELF peak is roughly half the plasma peak, ELF lags
plasma, and tazobactam declines faster than ceftolozane in both matrices.

## PKNCA: dose-3 exposure in plasma and ELF

The paper's comparator is the AUC ratio: geometric mean of the individual
Bayesian ELF:plasma AUC ratios 0.52 (ceftolozane) and 0.50 (tazobactam)
(Results), and the Discussion's terminal half-lives of about 2.5 h
(ceftolozane) and 1 h (tazobactam) in healthy volunteers.

```{r hv-pknca}
hv_conc <- hv |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Celf), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(drug, ifelse(matrix == "Cc", "plasma", "ELF"))) |>
  select(id, time, conc, treatment)
hv_dose <- hv_conc |>
  distinct(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(drug = sub(" .*", "", treatment)) |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = c(0, 8, 16)) |>
  mutate(amt = ifelse(drug == "ceftolozane", 1000, 500)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(hv_conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(hv_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 16, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

hv_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(drug = sub(" .*", "", treatment), matrix = sub(".* ", "", treatment)) |>
  select(id, drug, matrix, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(`geometric mean AUC ratio (simulated)` = exp(mean(log(ELF / plasma))))
hv_auc$`geometric mean (paper)` <- c(0.52, 0.50)
knitr::kable(hv_auc, digits = 3)
```

```{r hv-nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~half.life,
  "ceftolozane plasma", 2.5,
  "tazobactam plasma", 1.0
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "mg/L", auclast = "mg*h/L", tmax = "h", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated dose-3 NCA vs. the Discussion's half-lives. * differs from reference by >20%.")
```

```{r hv-gates}
stopifnot(
  # Geometric-mean AUC ratio within 0.08 of the paper's (its 95% CI half-widths
  # are 0.08 and 0.09). A mis-transcribed Qce or Qec moves it by 0.1 or more.
  abs(hv_auc$`geometric mean AUC ratio (simulated)` - hv_auc$`geometric mean (paper)`) < 0.08
)
```

The simulated ELF:plasma AUC ratios sit on the model's parametric PR (0.51,
0.46). The paper's tazobactam figure of 0.50 is the geometric mean of the
individual post-hoc ratios, which it reports as consistent with the parametric
0.46.

The tazobactam half-life matches the Discussion's "approximately 1 hour". The
ceftolozane half-life (about 1.9 h) is shorter than the Discussion's
"approximately 2.5 hours" (flagged above). That is a property of the Table 1
estimates themselves: CL = 6.3 L/h, Vc = 10.3 L, Q2 = 3.39 L/h and V2 = 3.76 L
give a terminal half-life of 1.85 h. The 2.5 h figure is quoted from a
separate multiple-dose study in healthy volunteers, not from this fit, so it is
not used as a gate.

# Part 2: simulation model for nosocomial pneumonia

## Virtual patients

200 virtual patients per scenario (the paper used 1000). CrCL is uniform on
the scenario's range and body weight is normal with mean 74 kg and the paper's
printed spread of 0.205 kg. Five scenarios are simulated to steady state
(seventh dose, 48-56 h).

```{r np-cohort}
n_np <- 200
np_events <- function(dose, crcl_lo, crcl_hi, scenario, id_offset) {
  cov <- data.frame(
    id = id_offset + seq_len(n_np),
    CRCL = runif(n_np, crcl_lo, crcl_hi),
    WT = rnorm(n_np, 74, 0.205)
  )
  bind_rows(
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, time = seq(0, 48, by = 8)) |>
      mutate(amt = dose, rate = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_),
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = cov$id, time = seq(48, 56, by = 0.05)) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  ) |>
    left_join(cov, by = "id") |>
    mutate(scenario = scenario) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
np_solve <- function(model, events) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(ui[[model]], events, keep = "scenario", returnType = "data.frame") |>
    filter(time >= 48) |>
    mutate(tad = time - 48)
}
cef <- bind_rows(
  np_solve("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia", np_events(2000, 90, 150, "3 g, normal", 0L)),
  np_solve("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia", np_events(1000, 90, 150, "1.5 g, normal", 1000L)),
  np_solve("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia", np_events(1000, 30, 50, "1.5 g, moderate RI", 2000L)),
  np_solve("Xiao_2016_ceftolozane_pneumonia", np_events(500, 15, 30, "750 mg, severe RI", 3000L))
)
taz <- np_solve("Xiao_2016_tazobactam_pneumonia", np_events(1000, 90, 150, "3 g, normal", 4000L))
```

## Figure 4: steady-state profiles at 3 g every 8 hours

```{r fig4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Xiao 2016: simulated steady-state plasma and ELF concentrations after 3 g ceftolozane/tazobactam (2000/1000 mg) as a 60-minute infusion every 8 hours, normal renal function (median and 5th-95th percentiles of 200 virtual patients)."}
fig4 <- bind_rows(
  cef |> filter(scenario == "3 g, normal") |> mutate(drug = "ceftolozane"),
  taz |> mutate(drug = "tazobactam")
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Celf), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(matrix = ifelse(matrix == "Cc", "Plasma", "ELF")) |>
  group_by(drug, matrix, tad) |>
  summarise(p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop")
ggplot(fig4, aes(tad, p50, colour = matrix, fill = matrix)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since last dose (h)", y = "Concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

The median peaks read from Figure 4 by the maintainers are about 98 mg/L
(ceftolozane plasma), 38 mg/L (ceftolozane ELF), 28 mg/L (tazobactam plasma)
and 9 mg/L (tazobactam ELF).

```{r fig4-gate}
peaks <- fig4 |>
  group_by(drug, matrix) |>
  summarise(median_peak = max(p50), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(figure4 = c(38, 98, 9, 28)[match(paste(drug, matrix),
    c("ceftolozane ELF", "ceftolozane Plasma", "tazobactam ELF", "tazobactam Plasma"))],
    pct_diff = 100 * (median_peak / figure4 - 1))
knitr::kable(peaks, digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  nrow(peaks) == 4,
  # Read off a log axis, about +/-10%. The printed (shift-free) tazobactam Vc
  # equation gives a plasma median peak near 34 mg/L, +20%.
  all(abs(peaks$pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

## Figures 5 and 7: probability of target attainment

%fT>MIC is the fraction of the steady-state dosing interval during which the
unbound concentration exceeds the MIC. In plasma the paper's unbound fractions
are applied (0.79 ceftolozane, 0.70 tazobactam). In ELF the total
concentration is used: that is the reading under which the model reproduces
the paper's ELF figures (with 0.79 applied in ELF the 3 g, 1-log-kill PTA at
MIC 8 mg/L falls to about 95% against the paper's 98.4%), and ELF is commonly
taken as essentially protein-free.

```{r pta}
pta <- function(sim, col, fu, mic, target) {
  sim |>
    group_by(scenario, id) |>
    summarise(ft = 100 * mean(fu * .data[[col]][tad > 0] > mic), .groups = "drop") |>
    group_by(scenario) |>
    summarise(pta = 100 * mean(ft >= target), .groups = "drop")
}
claims <- tribble(
  ~drug, ~scenario, ~matrix, ~target, ~mic, ~paper, ~source,
  "ceftolozane", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 32.2, 8, 98.4, "Results text",
  "ceftolozane", "3 g, normal", "plasma", 32.2, 16, 97.1, "Results text",
  "ceftolozane", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 40, 8, 95.6, "Results text",
  "ceftolozane", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 50, 8, 87.7, "Results text",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "plasma", 20, 2, 96, "Figure 7A (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "plasma", 20, 4, 88, "Figure 7A (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "plasma", 40, 1, 81, "Figure 7A (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "plasma", 40, 2, 66, "Figure 7A (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 20, 4, 73, "Figure 7B (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 20, 8, 33, "Figure 7B (read)",
  "tazobactam", "3 g, normal", "ELF", 40, 2, 62, "Figure 7B (read)",
  "ceftolozane", "1.5 g, normal", "ELF", 32.2, 8, 85, "Results text ('approximately')",
  "ceftolozane", "1.5 g, normal", "plasma", 32.2, 16, 74, "Results text ('approximately')",
  "ceftolozane", "1.5 g, normal", "ELF", 50, 8, 59, "Results text and Discussion",
  "ceftolozane", "1.5 g, moderate RI", "ELF", 32.2, 8, 98.8, "Results text",
  "ceftolozane", "750 mg, severe RI", "ELF", 32.2, 8, 94.4, "Results text"
)
fu <- c(ceftolozane = 0.79, tazobactam = 0.70)
claims$model <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(claims)), function(i) {
  r <- claims[i, ]
  sim <- if (r$drug == "ceftolozane") cef else taz
  res <- pta(filter(sim, scenario == r$scenario),
             col = ifelse(r$matrix == "ELF", "Celf", "Cc"),
             fu = ifelse(r$matrix == "ELF", 1, fu[[r$drug]]),
             mic = r$mic, target = r$target)
  if (nrow(res) != 1L) stop("no unique PTA for row ", i)
  res$pta
}, numeric(1))
# The two 1.5 g 1-log-kill values are inconsistent with the paper's own 3 g
# figures under linear PK (see Assumptions); shown, but not gated.
claims$deviation <- claims$scenario == "1.5 g, normal" & claims$target == 32.2
claims$diff <- claims$model - claims$paper
knitr::kable(claims, digits = 1,
             caption = "PTA (%) of the packaged simulation models vs. Xiao 2016. 'deviation' rows are documented below and excluded from the gate.")
stopifnot(
  sum(!claims$deviation) == 14,
  # 200 patients: binomial SE <= 3.5 points at PTA 50-90%; figure reading +/-3.
  # The printed shift-free tazobactam Vc moves the Figure 7A rows by 7-9 points
  # and the plasma unbound fraction applied in ELF moves the ELF rows by 3-15.
  all(abs(claims$diff[!claims$deviation]) < 10)
)
```

All eleven 3 g targets are reproduced, as are the renal-impairment values
(the paper's 98.8% for 1.5 g at CrCL 30-50 mL/min and 94.4% for 750 mg at
CrCL 15-30 mL/min, 1-log kill at MIC 8 mg/L in ELF) and the 1.5 g value for
50% fT>MIC. For
tazobactam, the printed `Vc`
equation without the cIAI shift (see Assumptions) gives plasma PTAs 5-10
points lower than Figure 7A (for example about 72% instead of 81% for 40%
fT>MEC at 1 mg/L).

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Tazobactam pneumonia `Vc` equation.** The paper prints
  `Vc=14.2*exp[N(0, 0.387)]`. Every other printed variance equals the square of
  the corresponding Chandorkar 2015 CV (0.330^2 = 0.109, 0.398^2 = 0.158,
  0.502^2 = 0.252), and exp(0.387) = 1.47 is Chandorkar 2015's cIAI factor on
  tazobactam `Vc` (Table 3B). The paper also states that the cIAI-patient
  parameters were used for the plasma PK. The maintainers therefore read the
  equation as `14.2*exp[0.387 + N(0, 0.2756)]`, with the variance 0.525^2 from
  Chandorkar 2015's 52.5% BSV. The cIAI shift is required to reproduce the
  median peaks of Figure 4B and the plasma PTAs of Figure 7A; the variance
  could not be told apart from the printed 0.387 with those figures.
- **Ceftolozane pneumonia `CL` variance.** Printed as `N(0, 109)`; read as
  0.109 (= 0.330^2, Chandorkar 2015's 33.0% BSV). A variance of 109 is
  impossible for a log-normal clearance.
- **cIAI shifts on the typical values.** The printed coefficients 0.195
  (ceftolozane CL), 0.464 (ceftolozane Vc) and 0.387 (tazobactam Vc) are the
  log-scale cIAI effects of Chandorkar 2015 (exp: 1.22, 1.59, 1.47) and are
  applied to every simulated patient.
- **Ceftolozane pneumonia weight effect.** Chandorkar 2015 switches the
  weight effect on ceftolozane Vc off in cIAI patients; Xiao 2016's
  simulation equation keeps `(WT/74)`. The Xiao form is packaged. With weight
  sampled tightly around 74 kg it makes no difference to the simulations.
- **Central-compartment equation.** The printed `dXc/dt` has `Q2/Vc X2` for
  the return from the peripheral compartment; the peripheral equation has
  `Q2/V2 X2`. The mass-balance form `Q2/V2` is packaged.
- **Tazobactam healthy-volunteer weight effect.** Table 1 gives `Vc` "at 70-kg
  body weight" and lists no weight exponent among the estimates, so the
  exponent was not estimated; it is packaged as fixed proportional scaling,
  `(WT/70)^1`.
- **Residual error.** Table 1 gives one residual model per drug; it is applied
  to both plasma and ELF (as separate `Cc` and `Celf` parameters with the same
  values). The simulation models carry no residual error (`fixed(0)`), as none
  was specified for the PTA simulations.
- **All simulation-model values are fixed.** They were carried from the two
  component models rather than estimated, so every `ini()` entry of the two
  `_pneumonia` models is wrapped in `fixed()`.
- **Unbound fraction in ELF.** Not stated; total ELF concentration reproduces
  the paper's ELF PTAs, while applying the plasma unbound fraction does not
  (see the PTA section).
- **1.5 g, 1-log-kill PTAs (not reproduced).** The model is linear,
  so PTA at 1.5 g and MIC 8 mg/L must equal PTA at 3 g and MIC 16 mg/L in the
  same population. The paper's own figures break that identity: for 1-log kill
  in ELF, Figure 5B (3 g) at MIC 16 reads about 80% while Figure 6B (1.5 g) at
  MIC 8 reads about 85%, which is also the value the Results quote
  ("approximately 85%"; the Discussion says 88%). In plasma, Figure 5A at
  MIC 32 reads about 63% against the Results' "approximately 74%" at 1.5 g and
  MIC 16. The packaged model agrees with the 3 g figures (all eleven targets
  above) and so falls below these two 1.5 g values, by about 7 and 11 points
  in this cohort. No published detail explains the difference; the two rows
  are shown and excluded from the gate.
- **Virtual cohorts.** The healthy-volunteer cohort draws CrCL and weight
  uniformly over the published ranges (only medians and ranges were
  reported). The pneumonia cohorts use 200 patients per scenario instead of
  the paper's 1000.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found on EuropePMC
  (checked 2026-11-24). The article has no supplementary material.
